leads.title: Act on the Prohibition of Discrimination on the grounds of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Gender Expression (Lov om forbud mot diskriminering på grunn av seksuell orientering, kjønnsidentitet og kjønnsuttrykk) - 2013
leads.documents: Legal prohibition of discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression, including definition of direct/indirect differential treatment
leads.detail: Enacted 2013; Section 5 quoted in article; protects actual, assumed, former or future orientation/identity/expression; also noted as explicitly protecting intersex people

leads.title: Norwegian Penal Code Paragraph 349a and Paragraph 135a amendments + 2020 amendment
leads.documents: Criminal anti-discrimination (1981) and hate speech protections; extension to bisexual and transgender people
leads.detail: 1981: Norway first to enact law preventing discrimination in goods/services/public gatherings (349a) and hate speech on account of sexual orientation (135a); Employment discrimination banned since 1998; November 2020 Storting amended hate speech law to protect bisexual and transgender people

leads.title: Solberg Government Legal Gender Change Law - approved 6 June 2016, effective 1 July 2016
leads.documents: Self-determination model for legal sex change without psychiatric/psychological evaluation, diagnosis or medical intervention
leads.detail: Bill introduced 18 March 2016; age 16+ self-declare, ages 6-16 with parental consent; passed 79-13; promulgated 17 June; 190 applications in first month

leads.title: Norwegian Conversion Therapy Ban - approved 12 December 2023, effective 1 January 2024
leads.detail: Parliament vote 85-15; under discussion since December 2019; substantive Storting discussion delayed until Autumn April-June 2023; Norwegian Psychiatric Association 2000 position statement cited as background that homosexuality is no disorder

leads.title: Oslo Police District - bias-motivated crimes statistics 2018
leads.documents: Enforcement data on hate crime in Oslo, including share related to LGBT status
leads.detail: 238 bias-motivated crimes in Oslo in 2018, of which 20 percent related to LGBT status; remainder ethnicity 57%, religion 17%, disability 3%, anti-Semitism 3%

leads.title: Norwegian Institute of Social Research - 2019 report on hate speech
leads.documents: Disparate risk of hate speech/threats for LGBT people vs general population
leads.detail: Reported 2019: 15% of LGBT respondents target of personal threats, mostly online, compared to 4% among general population

leads.title: University of Bergen - 'Sexual orientation and living conditions' (Seksuell orientering og levekår) 2013 survey
leads.documents: Workplace discrimination, physical assault, suicide trends, and school bullying for LGBT people
leads.detail: Nine of ten LGBT respondents not exposed to workplace discrimination/harassment; small minority physically assaulted; suicide decreased since 1990s; homosexual boys 6x higher school bullying than heterosexual boys

leads.title: Norwegian Directorate for Health - 2020 guideline for gender incongruence
leads.documents: Governmental health guideline on access to gender-affirming healthcare including puberty blockers
leads.detail: Recommends puberty blockers between Tanner stage 2 and age 16 following interdisciplinary assessment, stating reversible and no reliable evidence of adverse long-term effects; notes access still requires psychiatric diagnosis and referral to National Treatment Centre for Gender Incongruence (NTCGI) at Oslo University Hospital

leads.title: Norwegian Directorate for Children, Youth and Family Affairs (Bufdir) - attitude survey and March 2019 intersex reports
leads.documents: Official tracking of hostile attitudes toward gay/trans people and recommendation to postpone intersex infant surgeries until consent
leads.detail: 2017 finding: 7.8% hostile attitudes toward gay people, 11% toward transgender people, steadily decreasing; March 2019 published two reports recommending postponing medical interventions on intersex infants; related 2019 Oslo University Hospital survey: 2 of 3 medical professionals willing to perform such surgeries

leads.title: Extremism Commission's report + Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre 22 July anniversary speech
leads.documents: Institutional documentation of virulent incitement/hate, threats and violence targeting queer and especially trans people, and links between radical feminism and Christian conservatism in anti-trans activism
leads.detail: Report cited as noting groups using violent/dehumanizing language; PM statement: 'we know that queer people are the targets of hate, threats and violence. The incitement of hate is especially virulent against trans people'
